To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the molecular interactions of the cyanobacteria circadian clock proteins KaiC, KaiA and KaiB are revealed by structural characterization of stoichiometric assemblies of the purified proteins.

the cyanobacterial clock proteins KaiC, KaiA, and KaiB form a dynamic molecular oscillator that is capable of autonomous ticking in vitro in the presence of ATP, that this system can be studied by single-particle electron cryomicroscopy and mass spectrometric analysis, and that this analysis provides a structural explanation for the assembly and disassembly cycles of the oscillator.

the molecular structure of the cyanobacteria circadian oscillator can be frozen in a fully functional state, and that the structure of the oscillator is consistent with the known biochemical properties of the Kai proteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the molecular mechanisms underlying the biological clock in cyanobacteria.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the circadian clockwork of the cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942.
the molecular mechanism of the circadian oscillator of the unicellular cyanobacterium Synechococcus elongatus PCC 7942.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“we are now beginning to understand the mechanism of the cyanobacteria clock”.
the molecular clockwork is a complex system with many moving parts.
the cyanobacterial clockwork, the so-called Kai clock, is a robust and highly dynamic molecular oscillator.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have been able to determine the structure of the cyanobacteria clockwork, which is the core of the circadian oscillator.
we solved the crystal structure and the solution structure of a fully assembled cyanobacterial clock.
the structure of the cyanobacteria circadian oscillator is now known.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cyanobacterial KaiCBA complex has a structure similar to the one of the bacterial AAA+ ATPase complex Cdc48.
the Kai system is a complex of three different proteins that undergo a large number of conformational changes.
the cyanobacterial clock can be reconstiuited in vitro from just three proteins.
